messages.content: "Can you tell me the net worth of the famous footballer Lionel Messi in Euros? After that, I would like to know the net worth of the basketball player LeBron James in British Pounds. Also, I'm curious about the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person who weighs 85 kilograms and is 180 centimeters tall using the metric system. Lastly, could you calculate the BMI of another person who weighs 200 pounds and is 6 feet 2 inches tall using the imperial system?"

function.name: calculate_bmi
function.description: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

weight.description: Weight of the person in kilograms.

height.description: Height of the person in centimeters.

unit.description: Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'.

function.name: celebrity_net_worth_get
function.description: Get the total net worth of a sports celebrity based on most recent data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the sports celebrity.

currency.description: The currency in which the net worth will be returned. Default is 'USD'.

First request: net worth of Lionel Messi in Euros. So call celebrity_net_worth_get with name "Lionel Messi", currency "EUR".

Second request: net worth of LeBron James in British Pounds. So call celebrity_net_worth_get with name "LeBron James", currency "GBP".

Third request: BMI of person weighing 85 kg, height 180 cm, metric. So call calculate_bmi with weight=85, height=180, unit="metric". Actually default is metric, but we can specify.

Fourth request: BMI of person weighing 200 pounds, height 6 feet 2 inches tall, imperial. So weight=200, height=?? Height in centimeters? Wait calculate_bmi expects height in centimeters. But we have height in feet and inches. We need to convert to centimeters. 6 feet 2 inches = 6*12+2 = 74 inches. 1 inch = 2.54 cm. So height in cm = 74 * 2.54 = 187.96 cm. So height=187.96. Unit="imperial"? But the function's unit param chooses between 'imperial' and 'metric', default metric. If we pass unit='imperial', it might interpret weight in pounds and height in inches? But the function signature says weight in kilograms, height in centimeters. But optional unit param to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. So if we set unit='imperial', maybe the function expects weight in pounds and height in inches. But the description says weight in kilograms, height in centimeters. That seems contradictory. But likely the function can handle both units if unit specified. So we should pass weight=200, height=74, unit='imperial'. That matches typical usage: weight in pounds, height in inches. So we don't need to convert. But the user gave weight in pounds and height in feet and inches. So we can pass weight=200, height=74, unit='imperial'.

Thus calls:

1. celebrity_net_worth_get({"name":"Lionel Messi","currency":"EUR"})
2. celebrity_net_worth_get({"name":"LeBron James","currency":"GBP"})
3. calculate_bmi({"weight":85,"height":180,"unit":"metric"})
4. calculate_bmi({"weight":200,"height":74,"unit":"imperial"})
